title: New Study Finds Shocking Results for Organic Meat
summary: Reviews a German study finding organic meat no better than conventional meat for greenhouse gases, while organic plant foods score best.

assertions.quote: the organic meat based products are slightly higher in in most cases than the conventional meat based products in terms of emissions

verdicts.note: Life-cycle studies generally find organic meat's emissions per kilogram similar to or above conventional meat because of slower growth and more land use.

assertions.quote: the organic plant foods have half of the emissions on average as the conventionally grown plant foods

verdicts.note: Skipping synthetic nitrogen cuts emissions, but per-kilogram comparisons are mixed once lower yields and extra land are counted.

Across 44 paired organic-conventional LCAs, mostly crops, GHG per unit of food did not differ significantly (4% lower organic, p=0.59); the text gives no plant-only breakdown showing a reliable reduction.

assertions.quote: organic has higher land use per animal if they have lower productivity
three and a half times higher methane emissions for grass-fed cows versus grain fed cows

verdicts.note: Grass-finished cattle grow more slowly and produce more enteric methane per kilogram of beef, though soil carbon may offset part of it.

In 7 paired systems grass-fed beef had 19% higher GHG per unit food (not significant, p=0.22), which the authors attribute to slower growth and slaughter 6-12 months later raising lifetime methane; the direction fits, but the sample is small and the difference not significant.
